sources.text: UCSD Cosmology This is the home of the UCSD cosmology research group. We currently do research on the cosmic microwave background (CMB) and the near-infrared background (NIRB). For a list of the projects we are working on, go to the projects page. Brian Keating & Kam Arnold's Cosmology Group

sources.text: Current Projects The members of our group participate in a wide range of projects throughout the world. BICEP1 A CMB polarimeter that observed from 2006 to 2008 BICEP2 A CMB polarimeter that observed from 2010 to 2012 CIBER A rocket that is used to measure the near-IR background POLARBEAR A CMB polarimeter located in the Atacama desert in Chile Simons Array An array of 3 telescopes to be deployed in the Atacama desert Simons Observatory A new astronomy facility in Chile’s Atacama Desert that will merge and expand existing efforts Technology Transfer Instrumentation for astrophysics and beyond

sources.text: Faculty Astronomy & Astrophysics faculty pursue cutting-edge research at all scales of the Universe through instrumentation, observation, simulation, and theory. The A&A departmental faculty are included in the list below. Physics faculty that are active in the area of astrophysical research are Associate Professor Dan Green , Associate Professor Raphael Flaugher , Distinguished Professor George Fuller , Professor Brian Keating , and Associate Professor Tongyan Lin . Kam Arnold Associate Professor Kam Arnold develops technology for the next generation of detectors and telescopes to measure the intensity and polarization of the Cosmic Microwave Background. ksarnold[@]ucsd.edu Steven Boggs Professor Steven Boggs is an experimental astrophysicist specializing in the development of novel instrumentation and techniques to study nuclear astrophysics, particle astrophysics, and compact objects. seboggs[@]ucsd.edu Floor Broekgaarden Assistant Professor Floor Broekgaarden works in the intersection of data science, statistics, and astrophysics with a focus on developing the new frontier of "gravitational-wave paleontology": studying the formation, lives, and explosive deaths of massive stars across cosmic time from their “fossils” as black hole and neutron star mergers via gravitational waves. fbroekgaarden[@]ucsd.edu Adam Burgasser Professor Adam Burgasser applies observational techniques to discovering and characterizing the lowest-mass stars, brown dwarfs, and extrasolar planets. aburgasser[@]ucsd.edu Alison Coil Professor Alison Coil is an observational astrophysicist that specializes in understanding galaxy formation and evolution. acoil[@]ucsd.edu Patrick Diamond Distinguished Professor Pat Diamond is a theoretical physicist who specializes in nonlinear problems related to plasma and fluids, including turbulence, transport, and self-organization. pdiamond[@]physics.ucsd.edu Griffin Hosseinzadeh Assistant Professor Griffin Hosseinzadeh specializes in observations of explosive astronomical transients, particularly supernovae and kilonovae, which he uses to study the poorly understood late stages of stellar evolution. ghosseinzadeh[@]ucsd.edu Dusan Keres Professor Dusan Keres is a theoretical astrophysicist that specializes in using advanced simulations to understand galaxy formation and evolution. dkeres[@]physics.ucsd.edu Quinn Konopacky Professor Quinn Konopacky uses high resolution techniques on large ground based telescopes to study star and planet formation and evolution. Professor Konopacky is the Chair of the Department of Astronomy & Astrophysics. qkonopacky[@]ucsd.edu Kyle Kremer Assistant Professor Kyle Kremer is a theoretical astrophysicist specializing in compact objects, the dynamics of dense stellar systems like globular clusters, and the formation of gravitational wave sources and high energy transients. kykremer[@]ucsd.edu Eve Lee Associate Professor Eve J. Lee is a theoretical astrophysicist specializing in star and planet formation, using a wide range of tools from analytic calculations to numerical simulations. evelee[@]ucsd.edu Ethan Nadler Assistant Professor Ethan Nadler is a computational astrophysicist who specializes in galaxy formation, dark matter, and near-field cosmology, with a focus on cosmological simulations of dwarf galaxies and dark matter halos. enadler[@]ucsd.edu Michael Norman Distinguished Professor Mike Norman is a Professor of the Graduate Division who specializes in computational astrophysics, with programs in cosmology, galaxy formation, star formation, and high-energy astrophysics. mlnorman[@]ucsd.edu Karin Sandstrom Professor Karin Sandstrom is an observational astrophysicist that specializes in the interstellar medium, with a focus on dust properties and evolution in nearby galaxies. kmsandstrom[@]ucsd.edu Chris Theissen Assistant Professor Theissen explores the habitability of planets around the smallest stars by combining large survey datasets and machine learning methods to examine stellar and exoplanet demographics. ctheissen[@]ucsd.edu Samantha Trumbo Assistant Professor Samantha Trumbo is an astronomer and planetary scientist who studies the surfaces, atmospheres, and potential habitability of planetary bodies in the outer solar system using ground- and space-based telescopes and data from spacecraft exploration missions. sktrumbo[@]ucsd.edu David Tytler Professor David Tytler specializes in observational cosmology and new instrumentation, utilizing data from a range of large ground and spaced-based telescopes. dtytler[@]ucsd.edu Shelley Wright Professor Shelley Wright is an experimental and observational astrophysicist that specializes in optical and infrared instrumentation, galaxy formation and evolution, and technosignatures. s2wright[@]ucsd.edu Affiliate Faculty George Fuller Distinguished Professor George Fuller’s research revolves around theoretical nuclear and elementary particle physics and astrophysics, gravitation, and dark matter and cosmology. gfuller[@]ucsd.edu Emeritus Faculty Kim Griest Physics Emeritus Professor Kim Griest has worked in theoretical and experimental cosmology, for example, dark matter, dark energy, gravitational lensing, and extra-solar planets, as well other aspects of particle astrophysics and the early universe. kgriest[@]ucsd.edu Tom Murphy Emeritus Professor Murphy is an expert in astrophysics instrumentation and is known for his experiments with infrared spectroscopy of galaxies and for his precision lunar ranging tests to explore the principles of General Relativity. Professor Murphy has shifted his interests towards assessment of planetary limits and the fundamental mismatch between modernity’s demands and ecological sustainability. tmurphy[@]ucsd.edu
